rics.description: Industrial Production MM — Actual
rics.meaning: Actual month-on-month change in the Federal Reserve's Industrial Production Index, covering manufacturing, mining, and utilities output — released mid-month for the prior month.
rics.how_to_use: Broader than ISM surveys as it measures actual output volume; compare to ISM Manufacturing PMI (USPMI=ECI) to reconcile hard vs. soft data. A negative print confirms factory contraction signaled by sub-50 PMI readings.

rics.description: Industrial Production MM — Median Consensus
rics.meaning: Median Consensus forecast for Industrial Production MM from the Reuters economist poll, compiled ahead of the Fed's mid-month release.
rics.how_to_use: Benchmark for expected factory output; the actual-vs-median surprise is market-moving for industrials equities, USD, and rate expectations.

rics.description: Industrial Production MM — Mean Forecast
rics.meaning: Mean forecast for Industrial Production MM across all Reuters poll contributors.
rics.how_to_use: Compare with median to detect skew; a mean below median implies tail risk of a larger-than-expected output decline, consistent with energy or utility drag scenarios.

rics.description: Industrial Production MM — Mode Forecast
rics.meaning: Mode forecast for Industrial Production MM — the most frequently submitted individual estimate in the Reuters poll.
rics.how_to_use: Identifies the modal output growth scenario; useful when energy-sector surprises create a bimodal distribution in forecaster estimates.

rics.description: Industrial Production MM — Min Forecast
rics.meaning: Minimum individual forecast for Industrial Production MM — the most pessimistic output view in the Reuters poll.
rics.how_to_use: Defines the downside risk for output; a print at or below this level implies a significant industrial recession signal, likely to weigh on cyclical assets.

rics.description: Industrial Production MM — Max Forecast
rics.meaning: Maximum individual forecast for Industrial Production MM — the most optimistic output view in the Reuters poll.
rics.how_to_use: Defines the upside risk; a print above this level would be a strong beat on hard industrial data, supporting broader cyclical equity rotation.

rics.description: Industrial Production MM — Forecast Standard Deviation
rics.meaning: Standard deviation of all individual forecasts for Industrial Production MM — measures disagreement on the pace of output growth.
rics.how_to_use: High dispersion before the release suggests elevated uncertainty — often tied to energy sector volatility or weather distortions in utilities output.

rics.description: Industrial Production MM — SmartEconomics Forecast
rics.meaning: SmartEconomics machine-learning forecast for Industrial Production MM, incorporating energy output, manufacturing hours, and utility consumption signals.
rics.how_to_use: A model forecast diverging from street median (pUSIP=M) flags potential for an outsized Industrial Production surprise.

rics.description: Industrial Production MM — Predicted Surprise
rics.meaning: Predicted Surprise for Industrial Production MM — SmartEconomics' estimate of whether the actual will beat or miss the street consensus.
rics.how_to_use: A positive predicted surprise is bullish for manufacturing-sector equities, commodities, and cyclical currencies; use alongside ISM surprises for macro consistency checks.

rics.description: Industrial Production MM — Number of Forecasters
rics.meaning: Number of economists who submitted a forecast for Industrial Production MM in the current Reuters poll.
rics.how_to_use: A large, stable panel count confirms the median as a reliable consensus signal for this important hard-data release.

rics.description: ISM Manuf Employment Idx — Actual
rics.meaning: Actual release of the ISM Manufacturing Employment sub-index, measuring net hiring/firing intentions across ~300 surveyed manufacturing firms.
rics.how_to_use: Leads Nonfarm Payrolls for the manufacturing sector; a sustained move below 50 is an early warning of factory-sector job losses before the BLS print.

rics.description: ISM Manuf Employment Idx — Median Consensus
rics.meaning: Median Consensus forecast for the ISM Manufacturing Employment Index from the Reuters economist poll.
rics.how_to_use: Sets the expected baseline; surprise relative to consensus refines the pre-NFP labor market read for the manufacturing sector.

rics.description: ISM Manuf Employment Idx — Mean Forecast
rics.meaning: Mean forecast for the ISM Manufacturing Employment Index across all Reuters poll contributors.
rics.how_to_use: Compare with median (pUSISME=M) to detect skew; a mean below median implies tail risk of a negative labor-market surprise in manufacturing.

rics.description: ISM Manuf Employment Idx — Mode Forecast
rics.meaning: Mode forecast for the ISM Manufacturing Employment Index — the most frequently submitted value in the poll.
rics.how_to_use: Identifies the most common scenario among forecasters; useful when the distribution is bimodal and mean/median do not clearly represent the consensus.

rics.description: ISM Manuf Employment Idx — Min Forecast
rics.meaning: Minimum (most pessimistic) individual forecast for the ISM Manufacturing Employment Index in the Reuters poll.
rics.how_to_use: Defines the downside boundary; a print near or below this level indicates a severe manufacturing labor-market miss relative to all surveyed economists.

rics.description: ISM Manuf Employment Idx — Max Forecast
rics.meaning: Maximum (most optimistic) individual forecast for the ISM Manufacturing Employment Index in the Reuters poll.
rics.how_to_use: Defines the upside boundary; a print above this signals an outsized beat — likely to drive a stronger-than-expected reaction in rate and FX markets.

rics.description: ISM Manuf Employment Idx — Forecast Standard Deviation
rics.meaning: Standard deviation of all individual forecasts for the ISM Manufacturing Employment Index — measures economist disagreement.
rics.how_to_use: Rising dispersion ahead of the release signals elevated uncertainty about factory hiring conditions; consider widening risk bounds in pre-NFP models.

rics.description: ISM Manuf Employment Idx — SmartEconomics Forecast
rics.meaning: SmartEconomics machine-learning forecast for the ISM Manufacturing Employment Index.
rics.how_to_use: Compare to Median Consensus (pUSISME=M) for model-vs-street divergence; a gap above consensus may pre-signal better factory hiring than the street expects.

rics.description: ISM Manuf Employment Idx — Predicted Surprise
rics.meaning: Predicted Surprise for the ISM Manufacturing Employment Index — SmartEconomics' estimate of the likely deviation from street consensus.
rics.how_to_use: Use to adjust directional bias on the ISM Employment sub-index before release; feeds into pre-NFP positioning for manufacturing payrolls.

rics.description: ISM Manuf Employment Idx — Number of Forecasters
rics.meaning: Number of economists who submitted a forecast for the ISM Manufacturing Employment Index in the current Reuters poll.
rics.how_to_use: Low participation may indicate limited forecaster coverage of this sub-index; treat consensus with lower confidence when the count is well below average.

rics.description: ISM Manufacturing PMI — Actual
rics.meaning: Actual release of ISM Manufacturing PMI — the headline diffusion index from the Institute for Supply Management's survey of ~300 manufacturing firms. Released first business day of each month at 10:00 ET.
rics.how_to_use: Above 50 = expansion; sub-50 sustained signals manufacturing recession. Most-watched single business-cycle gauge in US data. Compare against Median Consensus (pUSPMI=M) — surprise drives Treasury yields, USD, and equity sector rotation.

rics.description: ISM Manufacturing PMI — Median Consensus
rics.meaning: Median Consensus forecast for ISM Manufacturing PMI from Reuters' poll of Wall Street economists, compiled ~1 week ahead of release.
rics.how_to_use: The 'expected' PMI. Markets trade the surprise (Actual minus Median). The 50 line is psychologically critical — consensus crossing back above signals a cycle inflection.

rics.description: ISM Manufacturing PMI — Mean Forecast
rics.meaning: Mean (arithmetic average) forecast for ISM Manufacturing PMI across all poll contributors, published alongside the median.
rics.how_to_use: Compare mean vs median — a large spread indicates skew in the distribution of forecasts, signaling asymmetric risk around the consensus view.

rics.description: ISM Manufacturing PMI — Mode Forecast
rics.meaning: Mode forecast for ISM Manufacturing PMI — the single most commonly submitted forecast value among poll participants.
rics.how_to_use: Shows where the largest cluster of forecasters sits; useful for identifying the 'modal scenario' when mean and median differ significantly.

rics.description: ISM Manufacturing PMI — Min Forecast
rics.meaning: Minimum (most bearish) individual forecast for ISM Manufacturing PMI submitted in the Reuters poll.
rics.how_to_use: Marks the bear-case boundary; if the actual print approaches or breaches this level it signals an outsized negative surprise.

rics.description: ISM Manufacturing PMI — Max Forecast
rics.meaning: Maximum (most bullish) individual forecast for ISM Manufacturing PMI submitted in the Reuters poll.
rics.how_to_use: Marks the bull-case boundary; use with pUSPMI=L to define the full forecast range and gauge how wide market uncertainty is ahead of the release.

rics.description: ISM Manufacturing PMI — Forecast Standard Deviation
rics.meaning: Standard deviation of all individual forecasts for ISM Manufacturing PMI in the Reuters poll — a direct measure of economist disagreement.
rics.how_to_use: Elevated standard deviation before a release implies higher macro uncertainty; options vol tends to be richer when forecast dispersion is wide.

rics.description: ISM Manufacturing PMI — SmartEconomics Forecast
rics.meaning: SmartEconomics machine-learning forecast for ISM Manufacturing PMI, generated by Refinitiv's quantitative model using macro leading indicators.
rics.how_to_use: Use alongside the Median Consensus (pUSPMI=M) to identify model-vs-street divergences; a large gap can signal an unusually directional risk ahead of the print.

rics.description: ISM Manufacturing PMI — Predicted Surprise
rics.meaning: Predicted Surprise for ISM Manufacturing PMI — SmartEconomics' estimate of the likely deviation between the actual release and the street consensus.
rics.how_to_use: A positive value implies the actual is likely to beat consensus; useful for pre-positioning or setting asymmetric options strategies around the release.

rics.description: ISM Manufacturing PMI — Number of Forecasters
rics.meaning: Number of economists who submitted a forecast for ISM Manufacturing PMI in the current Reuters poll.
rics.how_to_use: Higher participation increases consensus reliability; a low count relative to prior months may reflect unusual uncertainty or a thin pre-holiday survey.

rics.description: ISM Mfg Prices Paid — Actual
rics.meaning: Actual release of the ISM Manufacturing Prices Paid sub-index, measuring the net share of firms reporting higher input costs month-on-month.
rics.how_to_use: A leading indicator for goods-price inflation and PPI/CPI goods components; a surge above 60 has historically preceded rising core goods CPI by 1-3 months.

rics.description: ISM Mfg Prices Paid — Median Consensus
rics.meaning: Median Consensus forecast for ISM Manufacturing Prices Paid from the Reuters economist poll.
rics.how_to_use: Sets the inflation-signal baseline; a beat vs. consensus can shift breakeven inflation expectations and pressure the front-end of the rates curve.

rics.description: ISM Mfg Prices Paid — Mean Forecast
rics.meaning: Mean forecast for ISM Manufacturing Prices Paid across all Reuters poll contributors.
rics.how_to_use: Compare with median to detect distributional skew; an elevated mean relative to median suggests some forecasters see sharp cost-pressure acceleration.

rics.description: ISM Mfg Prices Paid — Mode Forecast
rics.meaning: Mode forecast for ISM Manufacturing Prices Paid — the most frequently submitted individual forecast in the poll.
rics.how_to_use: Identifies the modal price-pressure scenario; cross-reference with commodity futures trends to validate whether the consensus cluster makes sense.

rics.description: ISM Mfg Prices Paid — Min Forecast
rics.meaning: Minimum individual forecast for ISM Manufacturing Prices Paid in the Reuters poll — the most dovish cost-pressure view.
rics.how_to_use: Defines the downside scenario where input costs ease sharply; a print at or below this level signals unexpected goods deflation risk.

rics.description: ISM Mfg Prices Paid — Max Forecast
rics.meaning: Maximum individual forecast for ISM Manufacturing Prices Paid in the Reuters poll — the most hawkish cost-pressure view.
rics.how_to_use: Defines the upside scenario; a print above this level would represent a significant inflation shock from the manufacturing sector.

rics.description: ISM Mfg Prices Paid — Forecast Standard Deviation
rics.meaning: Standard deviation of all individual forecasts for ISM Manufacturing Prices Paid — a measure of disagreement on manufacturing inflation.
rics.how_to_use: High dispersion ahead of the release suggests commodity-price volatility is making inflation forecasting difficult; widen inflation risk premia accordingly.

rics.description: ISM Mfg Prices Paid — SmartEconomics Forecast
rics.meaning: SmartEconomics machine-learning forecast for ISM Manufacturing Prices Paid, incorporating commodity prices and pipeline inflation inputs.
rics.how_to_use: A model forecast above street median (pUSISMP=M) warns of underappreciated inflation pressure in manufacturing supply chains.

rics.description: ISM Mfg Prices Paid — Predicted Surprise
rics.meaning: Predicted Surprise for ISM Manufacturing Prices Paid — SmartEconomics' estimate of whether the actual will exceed or undershoot consensus.
rics.how_to_use: A positive predicted surprise in Prices Paid has hawkish implications; use as a pre-release signal for TIPS breakevens and USD positioning.

rics.description: ISM Mfg Prices Paid — Number of Forecasters
rics.meaning: Number of economists who submitted a forecast for ISM Manufacturing Prices Paid in the current Reuters poll.
rics.how_to_use: A larger panel provides more reliable consensus; a sharp drop in participant count may reduce confidence in the median forecast ahead of the release.

rics.description: ISM N-Mfg Bus Act — Actual
rics.meaning: Actual release of the ISM Non-Manufacturing Business Activity sub-index, which measures current output levels across services firms — the closest services equivalent to ISM Manufacturing Production.
rics.how_to_use: Often leads the headline Non-Manufacturing PMI at cycle turns; a sharp decline relative to consensus (pUSOPMI=M) signals abrupt softening in services output.

rics.description: ISM N-Mfg Bus Act — Median Consensus
rics.meaning: Median Consensus forecast for ISM Non-Manufacturing Business Activity from the Reuters economist poll.
rics.how_to_use: Sets the expected services output level; surprise vs. consensus can shift near-term GDP tracking estimates and broad risk-asset sentiment.

rics.description: ISM N-Mfg Bus Act — Mean Forecast
rics.meaning: Mean forecast for ISM Non-Manufacturing Business Activity across all Reuters poll contributors.
rics.how_to_use: Compare with median to detect skew; a mean significantly below median implies downside tail risk to services output — consider GDP tracking downside scenarios.

rics.description: ISM N-Mfg Bus Act — Mode Forecast
rics.meaning: Mode forecast for ISM Non-Manufacturing Business Activity — the most frequently submitted value in the poll.
rics.how_to_use: Reveals the modal output scenario; cross-check against current credit-card spending and retail data to validate the consensus cluster's plausibility.

rics.description: ISM N-Mfg Bus Act — Min Forecast
rics.meaning: Minimum individual forecast for ISM Non-Manufacturing Business Activity — the most bearish output view in the poll.
rics.how_to_use: Defines the downside risk boundary; a print at or below this level indicates a significant services output shock and will likely prompt downward GDP revisions.

rics.description: ISM N-Mfg Bus Act — Max Forecast
rics.meaning: Maximum individual forecast for ISM Non-Manufacturing Business Activity — the most bullish output view in the poll.
rics.how_to_use: Defines the upside risk boundary; a print above this implies exceptional services strength and is likely to trigger a broad risk-on move.

rics.description: ISM N-Mfg Bus Act — Forecast Standard Deviation
rics.meaning: Standard deviation of all individual forecasts for ISM Non-Manufacturing Business Activity — measures forecast dispersion.
rics.how_to_use: Elevated standard deviation signals uncertainty about near-term services output; corresponds to wider implied volatility on services-sensitive assets.

rics.description: ISM N-Mfg Bus Act — SmartEconomics Forecast
rics.meaning: SmartEconomics machine-learning forecast for ISM Non-Manufacturing Business Activity.
rics.how_to_use: Model divergence from street median (pUSOPMI=M) flags potential for an asymmetric services output surprise.

rics.description: ISM N-Mfg Bus Act — Predicted Surprise
rics.meaning: Predicted Surprise for ISM Non-Manufacturing Business Activity — SmartEconomics' estimate of whether the actual will beat or miss street consensus.
rics.how_to_use: A positive predicted surprise signals stronger-than-expected services output; bullish for consumer discretionary and rate-sensitive sectors.

rics.description: ISM N-Mfg Bus Act — Number of Forecasters
rics.meaning: Number of economists who submitted a forecast for ISM Non-Manufacturing Business Activity in the current Reuters poll.
rics.how_to_use: A stable, large panel count increases confidence in the consensus; a low or declining count raises questions about coverage and reliability of the median.

rics.description: ISM N-Mfg Employment Idx — Actual
rics.meaning: Actual release of the ISM Non-Manufacturing Employment sub-index, reflecting net hiring intentions in services-sector firms surveyed by ISM.
rics.how_to_use: A key early read on services-sector payrolls ahead of the monthly BLS report; sustained sub-50 readings flag deterioration in the dominant US employment sector.

rics.description: ISM N-Mfg Employment Idx — Median Consensus
rics.meaning: Median Consensus forecast for the ISM Non-Manufacturing Employment Index from the Reuters economist poll.
rics.how_to_use: Benchmark for expected services labor demand; a beat vs. consensus strengthens the pre-NFP bullish labor narrative and supports risk assets.

rics.description: ISM N-Mfg Employment Idx — Mean Forecast
rics.meaning: Mean forecast for the ISM Non-Manufacturing Employment Index across all Reuters poll contributors.
rics.how_to_use: Use alongside median to detect distributional asymmetry; a mean below the median signals a fatter left tail in services employment expectations.

rics.description: ISM N-Mfg Employment Idx — Mode Forecast
rics.meaning: Mode forecast for the ISM Non-Manufacturing Employment Index — the most frequently submitted individual estimate in the poll.
rics.how_to_use: Identifies the modal labor-demand scenario; useful when skewed distributions make the mean or median a poor representation of central tendency.

rics.description: ISM N-Mfg Employment Idx — Min Forecast
rics.meaning: Minimum individual forecast for the ISM Non-Manufacturing Employment Index in the Reuters poll.
rics.how_to_use: Sets the downside boundary for services hiring expectations; a print at or below this level implies a significant NFP downside risk in the services sector.

rics.description: ISM N-Mfg Employment Idx — Max Forecast
rics.meaning: Maximum individual forecast for the ISM Non-Manufacturing Employment Index in the Reuters poll.
rics.how_to_use: Sets the upside boundary for services hiring; a print above this level would be a strongly bullish pre-NFP signal.

rics.description: ISM N-Mfg Employment Idx — Forecast Standard Deviation
rics.meaning: Standard deviation of all individual forecasts for the ISM Non-Manufacturing Employment Index.
rics.how_to_use: Higher dispersion signals uncertainty about the services labor market ahead of the release; use to calibrate NFP forecast confidence intervals.

rics.description: ISM N-Mfg Employment Idx — SmartEconomics Forecast
rics.meaning: SmartEconomics machine-learning forecast for the ISM Non-Manufacturing Employment Index.
rics.how_to_use: Model forecast vs. street median (pUSEPMI=M) divergence highlights potential for upside or downside labor-market surprises in the services sector.

rics.description: ISM N-Mfg Employment Idx — Predicted Surprise
rics.meaning: Predicted Surprise for the ISM Non-Manufacturing Employment Index — SmartEconomics' estimate of actual minus consensus at release.
rics.how_to_use: Use ahead of the services PMI release as a directional bias signal for the employment sub-index; feeds into pre-NFP positioning.

rics.description: ISM N-Mfg Employment Idx — Number of Forecasters
rics.meaning: Number of economists who submitted a forecast for the ISM Non-Manufacturing Employment Index in the current Reuters poll.
rics.how_to_use: Low participation signals limited forecaster coverage of this sub-index; treat the consensus with appropriate caution when the count is well below historical norms.

rics.description: ISM N-Mfg PMI — Actual
rics.meaning: Actual release of the ISM Non-Manufacturing (Services) PMI — the headline composite index from ISM's survey of ~400 services-sector firms. Released third business day of each month at 10:00 ET.
rics.how_to_use: Services represent ~80% of US GDP, so this index is the dominant PMI for aggregate cycle tracking. A sustained move below 50 signals services recession; compare to pUSNPMI=M for the market-moving surprise.

rics.description: ISM N-Mfg PMI — Median Consensus
rics.meaning: Median Consensus forecast for ISM Non-Manufacturing PMI from Reuters' economist poll, published ~1 week before the release.
rics.how_to_use: Benchmark for the expected services activity level. The actual-vs-median surprise moves risk assets, particularly rate-sensitive equities and front-end Treasuries.

rics.description: ISM N-Mfg PMI — Mean Forecast
rics.meaning: Mean forecast for ISM Non-Manufacturing PMI across all Reuters poll contributors.
rics.how_to_use: Compare with median to detect skew; a mean well below median implies a fat left tail in the services activity distribution ahead of the release.

rics.description: ISM N-Mfg PMI — Mode Forecast
rics.meaning: Mode forecast for ISM Non-Manufacturing PMI — the most frequently submitted forecast value among poll participants.
rics.how_to_use: Reveals where the largest consensus cluster sits; useful when mean and median diverge and a clearer modal scenario is needed.

rics.description: ISM N-Mfg PMI — Min Forecast
rics.meaning: Minimum individual forecast for ISM Non-Manufacturing PMI — the bear-case floor in the Reuters poll.
rics.how_to_use: A print at or below this value signals an extreme negative surprise in services activity, consistent with rapid deterioration in the business cycle.

rics.description: ISM N-Mfg PMI — Max Forecast
rics.meaning: Maximum individual forecast for ISM Non-Manufacturing PMI — the bull-case ceiling in the Reuters poll.
rics.how_to_use: A print above this level indicates an exceptional beat; compare the range (H minus L) across months to track how uncertain forecasters are about services conditions.

rics.description: ISM N-Mfg PMI — Forecast Standard Deviation
rics.meaning: Standard deviation of all individual forecasts for ISM Non-Manufacturing PMI — a quantitative measure of forecast uncertainty.
rics.how_to_use: Elevated dispersion implies higher implied vol is warranted for rates and equity products sensitive to the services PMI release.

rics.description: ISM N-Mfg PMI — SmartEconomics Forecast
rics.meaning: SmartEconomics machine-learning forecast for ISM Non-Manufacturing PMI, using high-frequency consumption and services activity data.
rics.how_to_use: A model forecast diverging from street median (pUSNPMI=M) flags potential for a larger-than-expected surprise in the services sector.

rics.description: ISM N-Mfg PMI — Predicted Surprise
rics.meaning: Predicted Surprise for ISM Non-Manufacturing PMI — SmartEconomics' estimate of the likely deviation from the street consensus.
rics.how_to_use: A positive predicted surprise in services activity has bullish macro implications; trade-through into consumer discretionary equities and risk-on FX.

rics.description: ISM N-Mfg PMI — Number of Forecasters
rics.meaning: Number of economists who submitted a forecast for ISM Non-Manufacturing PMI in the current Reuters poll.
rics.how_to_use: Validates consensus reliability; a large, stable panel count increases confidence in the median as a clean market signal.

rics.description: KC Fed Composite Index — Actual
rics.meaning: Actual release of the Kansas City Fed Composite Activity Index, combining current conditions and future expectations of business activity across the 10th Fed District.
rics.how_to_use: The composite blends current activity with a forward-looking expectations component; use alongside the manufacturing sub-index (USKCMF=ECI) to distinguish momentum from direction.

rics.description: KC Fed Manufacturing — Actual
rics.meaning: Actual release of the Kansas City Fed Manufacturing Activity Index, a diffusion index of factory conditions across the 10th Federal Reserve District (Kansas, Colorado, Nebraska, and surrounding states).
rics.how_to_use: Regional Fed surveys supplement the national ISM; a consistent divergence between KC Fed and ISM Manufacturing (USPMI=ECI) highlights geographic variation in the industrial cycle.

rics.description: Manuf Output MM — Actual
rics.meaning: Actual month-on-month change in the manufacturing-only component of the Federal Reserve's Industrial Production Index, stripping out mining and utilities.
rics.how_to_use: Provides a cleaner read on factory sector health than total Industrial Production (USIP=ECI); compare to ISM Manufacturing PMI (USPMI=ECI) to reconcile survey vs. hard output data.

rics.description: Manuf Output MM — Median Consensus
rics.meaning: Median Consensus forecast for Manufacturing Output MM from the Reuters economist poll.
rics.how_to_use: Benchmark for expected factory output growth; a beat vs. consensus provides hard confirmation of what ISM surveys have been signaling about manufacturing conditions.

rics.description: Manuf Output MM — Mean Forecast
rics.meaning: Mean forecast for Manufacturing Output MM across all Reuters poll contributors.
rics.how_to_use: Compare with median to detect distributional skew; a lower mean relative to median implies downside tail risk to factory output growth.

rics.description: Manuf Output MM — Mode Forecast
rics.meaning: Mode forecast for Manufacturing Output MM — the most frequently submitted individual estimate in the poll.
rics.how_to_use: Reveals the modal factory output scenario; useful when auto-sector or supply-chain distortions create a bimodal forecast distribution.

rics.description: Manuf Output MM — Min Forecast
rics.meaning: Minimum individual forecast for Manufacturing Output MM — the most pessimistic factory output view in the Reuters poll.
rics.how_to_use: Defines the downside risk for manufacturing output; a print at or below this level confirms a severe factory contraction consistent with the bearish tail scenario.

rics.description: Manuf Output MM — Max Forecast
rics.meaning: Maximum individual forecast for Manufacturing Output MM — the most optimistic factory output view in the Reuters poll.
rics.how_to_use: Defines the upside risk boundary; a print above this level confirms strong manufacturing momentum and supports cyclical equity and commodity positions.

rics.description: Manuf Output MM — Forecast Standard Deviation
rics.meaning: Standard deviation of all individual forecasts for Manufacturing Output MM — measures forecast uncertainty around factory production.
rics.how_to_use: High dispersion suggests uncertainty about supply-chain and production conditions; use to calibrate width of confidence bands in manufacturing output models.

rics.description: Manuf Output MM — SmartEconomics Forecast
rics.meaning: SmartEconomics machine-learning forecast for Manufacturing Output MM.
rics.how_to_use: Use model divergence from street median (pUSFOUT=M) to identify potential hard-data surprises in the factory sector, particularly when ISM surveys diverge from output trends.

rics.description: Manuf Output MM — Predicted Surprise
rics.meaning: Predicted Surprise for Manufacturing Output MM — SmartEconomics' estimate of the likely deviation from street consensus at release.
rics.how_to_use: A positive predicted surprise strengthens the bullish manufacturing narrative; use in conjunction with ISM PMI surprises for a consistent cyclical sector view.

rics.description: Manuf Output MM — Number of Forecasters
rics.meaning: Number of economists who submitted a forecast for Manufacturing Output MM in the current Reuters poll.
rics.how_to_use: Validates the reliability of the consensus; a declining participant count may reflect reduced forecaster coverage of this sub-component relative to headline Industrial Production.

rics.description: NAHB Housing Market Indx — Actual
rics.meaning: Actual release of the NAHB/Wells Fargo Housing Market Index — a monthly survey of home builder sentiment scored 0-100, with 50 as the expansion/contraction threshold. Released mid-month, one day before Housing Starts.
rics.how_to_use: Leads housing starts by 1-2 months and is the primary real-time gauge of new residential construction demand; a sustained move below 50 signals housing sector weakness with implications for consumer spending and GDP.

rics.description: NAHB Housing Market Indx — Median Consensus
rics.meaning: Median Consensus forecast for the NAHB Housing Market Index from the Reuters economist poll.
rics.how_to_use: Sets the expected builder-sentiment baseline. A beat vs. consensus (USNAHB=ECI above pUSNAHB=M) is bullish for homebuilder equities and residential REITs.

rics.description: NAHB Housing Market Indx — Mean Forecast
rics.meaning: Mean forecast for the NAHB Housing Market Index across all Reuters poll contributors.
rics.how_to_use: Compare with median to detect distributional skew in housing sentiment expectations; a mean below median implies tail risk of a sharp builder confidence drop.

rics.description: NAHB Housing Market Indx — Mode Forecast
rics.meaning: Mode forecast for the NAHB Housing Market Index — the most frequently submitted estimate in the Reuters poll.
rics.how_to_use: Identifies the most common builder-sentiment scenario among forecasters; useful when mean and median are pulled apart by outlier estimates.

rics.description: NAHB Housing Market Indx — Min Forecast
rics.meaning: Minimum individual forecast for the NAHB Housing Market Index — the most pessimistic builder-sentiment view in the poll.
rics.how_to_use: Defines the downside risk for housing activity; a print at or below this level signals an outsized deterioration in builder confidence, bearish for homebuilder stocks.

rics.description: NAHB Housing Market Indx — Max Forecast
rics.meaning: Maximum individual forecast for the NAHB Housing Market Index — the most optimistic builder-sentiment view in the poll.
rics.how_to_use: Defines the upside risk; a print above this level represents a significant beat in housing conditions, likely to lift homebuilder equities sharply.

rics.description: NAHB Housing Market Indx — Forecast Standard Deviation
rics.meaning: Standard deviation of all individual forecasts for the NAHB Housing Market Index — a direct measure of forecast uncertainty.
rics.how_to_use: High dispersion signals elevated uncertainty about housing conditions — typically linked to sharp swings in mortgage rates; use to calibrate risk around the mid-month housing release.

rics.description: NAHB Housing Market Indx — SmartEconomics Forecast
rics.meaning: SmartEconomics machine-learning forecast for the NAHB Housing Market Index, incorporating mortgage rate trends and permit data.
rics.how_to_use: Model forecast vs. street median (pUSNAHB=M) divergence can signal unusual rate-sensitivity risk in builder sentiment ahead of the release.

rics.description: NAHB Housing Market Indx — Predicted Surprise
rics.meaning: Predicted Surprise for the NAHB Housing Market Index — SmartEconomics' estimate of whether the actual will beat or miss the street consensus.
rics.how_to_use: A positive predicted surprise implies stronger builder sentiment than expected; bullish for housing-related equities and mortgage-backed securities.

rics.description: NAHB Housing Market Indx — Number of Forecasters
rics.meaning: Number of economists who submitted a forecast for the NAHB Housing Market Index in the current Reuters poll.
rics.how_to_use: Higher participation validates the median as a robust consensus signal; a low count may reflect limited coverage of this housing indicator among poll participants.
